title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. The engines' own state is read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now. This article reports that state as it stands, in plain language, with no projection. A single trade says nothing about a strategy, and every position here is paper. The record is a description of recorded states, not an opinion about what will happen next.

## Framing and scope
The live record is paper only. v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026 and v006 from 9 October 2026. An ATOM entry at 2.066 came after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is −17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. In testing, losses were common and the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. The record is not a forecast and does not state what will happen next. It is a statement of recorded states, taken from the engines rather than from opinion. Paper signals only means the entries and exits are recorded states, not orders routed to an exchange. The live starts are the points from which these engines count their live record, and the closed-trade counts below are counted from those starts.

## Open positions
At the snapshot, htf-rsi-v007 has 0 positions open on paper. trend-daily-v005 has 0 positions open on paper. trend-daily-v006 has 0 positions open on paper. The only open position named in the record is NEAR, entered at 5.896 on 12 October 2026, which has been open since. All other named entries are closed. Because these are paper signals, an open position is a recorded state, not an instruction to act. A count of 0 is a state of the record, not a verdict on a method. Open positions are reported as counts and, where named, as entry price and date. NEAR remains open because no exit is recorded for it. The engines can hold 0 open positions while the market filter is off, and that combination is what the snapshot reports.

## Closed trades
htf-rsi-v007 has 4 closed trades so far, with an average of null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 has 6 closed trades so far, with an average of -13.22% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 has 7 closed trades so far, with an average of -13.34% net per trade. The ATOM trade exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close at 1.703, a result of −17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. These are realized paper outcomes. An average describes the closed trades that produced it, and it does not extend to trades that have not happened. A null average is also a reported value, not a missing explanation. The ATOM result includes the 30 bps round trip. A negative average across closed trades means the closed set, taken together, lost ground after costs. It does not predict the next closed trade.

## Market filter and nearest breakouts
trend-daily-v005 reports the Bitcoin market filter off. trend-daily-v006 reports the Bitcoin market filter off. The same snapshots report 0 positions open on paper for each trend engine. For trend-daily-v005, the names closest to their 20-day breakout are TRXUSDT at 13.34% below its high, XLMUSDT at 17.87% below its high, and AVAXUSDT at 18.82% below its high. For trend-daily-v006, the names closest to their 20-day breakout are JUPUSDT at 5.46% below its high, TRXUSDT at 13.34% below its high, and XLMUSDT at 17.87% below its high. These distances are measurements from the record. They show how far each named market is from its 20-day breakout level. A market that is below its high by a stated percentage has not reached the breakout level used by that engine. The list is ordered by closeness, with the smallest distance first. No entry is recorded for these markets in the snapshot. The filter state and the distances are reported together in the same snapshot.

## Where to check and how to read
The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. The record updates continuously, so the state read here is a snapshot rather than a final statement. Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. Read the figures as recorded states: open counts, closed counts, averages, filter state, and distances to breakouts. Do not treat a single trade, a single average, or a single snapshot as proof of a strategy. The performance page, the signal log, and the channel status are the places where the same numbers can be checked. The record updates continuously, and a later read can show a different state. Read the record as description, not as advice.
